notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 11.52 and later; operates on server package management.

The source requires exactly one selector family: namespaces or packages, each as one string or a nonempty sequential string list encoded with repeated ns or package keys. The source marks both required but explicitly makes them alternatives; both formal required flags conflict with the documented selector alternatives. Namespace prose permits ea and values returned by ea4_get_additional_pkg_prefixes, including the altea example, while the formal enum lists only ea. This discrepancy remains unresolved. Omitted disableExcludes preserves the default 0; explicit false sends 0. more_info_url may be null; omitted fields remain omitted.

Independent review clarification on 11.138.0.19 observed ea-apache24 requires containing strings and nested lists of strings (27 items, including two- or three-string alternatives), and vendor as a string on six packages. Conflicts remained strings. Four uninstalled packages returned version_installed as an empty string, while two installed packages returned nonempty strings; null was not observed and is not accepted.

The separately inspected package-manager source describes a requirement as a package name or an array reference of alternatives (an OR-list), and flattens conflicts to package-name strings. Nested requirement lists preserve alternative package strings, without an invented tuple or closed item count. The dnf vendor source uses a placeholder, so no vendor identity or literal value is guaranteed.

Caller responsibility: provide exactly one of namespaces or packages as required by the source. The client makes each individually optional so either family is callable; it does not reject an omitted selector or both families locally. This is not a guarantee that such calls succeed on the server.

notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 11.52 and later; operates on server package management.

Queues package installation, removal and upgrades as background tasks. Each action family is optional; omit it for no action of that kind, or pass one string or a nonempty sequential string list with repeated identical keys. The returned build is a process ID; API success does not establish completion. The client does not poll, retry or roll back package changes.

Caller responsibility: supply the intended nonempty package actions before calling. The client has no nonempty combination guard: omitted actions POST an empty body, and empty scalar strings are sent unchanged; empty lists are rejected locally. Do not rely on server rejection or assume an empty submission is harmless or a no-op. A returned build does not establish successful package changes.

install: omission sends no parameter for this family; an empty string is still sent. Supply an intended package name or nonempty string list; the client does not enforce a nonempty scalar or a nonempty combination of action families.

uninstall: omission sends no parameter for this family; an empty string is still sent. Supply an intended package name or nonempty string list; the client does not enforce a nonempty scalar or a nonempty combination of action families.

upgrade: omission sends no parameter for this family; an empty string is still sent. Supply an intended package name or nonempty string list; the client does not enforce a nonempty scalar or a nonempty combination of action families.
